pages.title: Getting started
pages.summary: Start Latchkey on your own computer in two lines, sign in as the owner and finish setup, and see what this release does.

pages.title: Your first vault
pages.summary: Register the command-line client, create a client-encrypted vault, store an item and read it back.

pages.title: Share a vault, remove someone
pages.summary: Compare fingerprints, share a vault with separate rights for each person, and change its keys when someone leaves.

pages.title: Devices, recovery and passwords
pages.summary: Approve a new device from one you trust, revoke a lost one, recover with your kit and change your password.

pages.title: Give a machine one secret
pages.summary: Let a server or deploy job read one item for up to an hour without holding your account or vault keys.

pages.title: Command reference
pages.summary: Every command of the vault client, its input fields and what it writes.

pages.title: Back up and restore
pages.summary: Back up the whole installation with rer, restore it into an empty one, and keep a vault export only you can open.

pages.title: Security design
pages.summary: The keys, the envelope format, request authority, devices and recovery, and the machine boundary, as the code implements them today.

pages.title: Threat model
pages.summary: What each boundary protects against today, its limits, and the independent review still to come.
